title: Where DNA and RNA sit inside RNA polymerase
topic: Explain to a learner who knows DNA stores a sequence and RNA is a copy how DNA and RNA are spatially organized within the large E. coli RNA polymerase transcription initiation complex represented by PDB 4YLN. Use the deposited structure as a static example, respect its limitations, and distinguish the protein machinery, DNA and RNA. Choose the representations that best reveal their spatial relationship, allowing the learner to make a guided observation before explaining it. Do not imply that a static structure demonstrates catalytic chemistry or motion. Make two connected scenes, about 60–90 seconds total. Deliver subtitles only.
